How to become a doctor in the UK

Explore UK medical school entry, A-level subjects, the UCAT, the Foundation Programme and specialty training, with an Oxford course example.

What subjects do you need?

Requirements depend on the medical school. Oxford requires chemistry and at least one of biology, physics or mathematics. It also requires the UCAT. For that test you practise reasoning with text and numbers, decision making, and judging behaviour in a given situation.

Oxford requirements · UCAT format
Admission
The standard route starts with medical school admission after secondary school. Graduate-entry programmes are also available to people who already hold a degree.
Medical school
Medical degrees normally take five years. Graduate-entry medicine usually takes four years from admission to medical school.
Licence to practise
After graduation, provisional General Medical Council registration allows doctors to start Foundation Year 1 (F1). Successfully completing F1 allows full registration and progression to F2.
Specialty training
After the two-year Foundation Programme, doctors can apply for general practice or other specialty training.
GMC · training pathway

Oxford · United Kingdom

On the standard A100 course, early blocks pair biochemistry with medical genetics and physiology with pharmacology. The Patient and Doctor course runs alongside them. Students also complete a research project during the first three years. The main clinical phase spans years 4–6, with medicine and surgery rotations in year 4.
